clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Aortic Dissection.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

safety_notes: Misclassification as ACS can lead to harmful antithrombotic or thrombolytic exposure.

basic_info.working_definition: Aortic dissection is a tear in the aortic intima with blood entering the media, creating a false lumen; it is an acute aortic syndrome when presenting abruptly.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Symptoms can mimic ACS, PE, stroke, abdominal emergencies, or musculoskeletal pain.
Pain can be chest, back, abdominal, migrating, or absent in some patients.
Neurologic symptoms, syncope, limb ischemia, or myocardial ischemia may dominate the presentation.
Delay in imaging and surgical referral for type A dissection is life-threatening.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Suspected acute aortic dissection requires immediate risk assessment, blood pressure/heart-rate control when appropriate, and urgent aortic imaging and surgical/endovascular consultation based on location.

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Abrupt severe chest/back/abdominal pain, syncope, neurologic deficit, pulse/BP differential, malperfusion, or high-risk aortic condition.

strong_activation_patterns.reason: Classic acute aortic syndrome pain pattern.

case_features: known aneurysm or connective tissue disease
back pain without abrupt severity or risk features
weak_activation_patterns.reason: Back pain is common and nonspecific.

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are high-risk pain features present: abrupt, severe, tearing/ripping, chest/back/abdominal, or migrating?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Increase suspicion and proceed toward urgent imaging.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Pain pattern less supportive but does not exclude.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are pulse deficit, BP differential, neuro deficit, aortic regurgitation, hypotension, shock, or malperfusion present?
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Exam data missing; cannot down-rank safely.

guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If imaging negative and quality adequate, consider alternatives.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Aortic dissection cannot be confirmed/excluded without appropriate imaging.

guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Type A pathway; urgent surgical consultation.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Type B pathway if descending only; evaluate complications.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are coronary, cerebral, spinal, visceral, renal, or limb malperfusion features present?
Could the presentation be ACS, PE, stroke, or another emergency, and are treatments potentially harmful if dissection is missed?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Report high-risk competing diagnoses and avoid premature closure.

distinguishing_features: Chest pain and ECG/troponin abnormalities may occur with coronary malperfusion.
Pulse/BP differential and abrupt tearing pain favor dissection.
Dyspnea, syncope, chest pain overlap; PE has VTE risk and CTPA findings.
Focal deficits may be due to carotid/aortic dissection extension; chest/back pain or pulse deficit is a clue.
Sudden pleuritic pain/dyspnea with unilateral breath findings.
Chest pain after vomiting, sepsis, mediastinal air.
Severe abdominal pain and lactate; can be caused by dissection malperfusion.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease
evidence_sources.publisher: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association
key_points: Includes diagnosis and management recommendations for acute aortic syndromes.
Supports high-risk condition, pain, examination-feature assessment and urgent aortic imaging when acute aortic syndrome is suspected.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not treat chest pain as ACS without considering dissection red flags.
Do not exclude dissection using chest radiograph alone.
Do not use D-dimer as a standalone rule-out in high-risk presentations.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always assess high-risk condition, high-risk pain, and high-risk exam features.
Always report whether definitive aortic imaging is available.
